threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver yells, 'Last stop!' while the rest of us grab our bags and head for the door.
Saw a bloke on the 59 last night trying to impress a girl with a magic trick, ended up spilling his drink all over her lap instead.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I spotted a family of raccoons raiding the bakery's trash at dawn, nonchalantly strolling down the street like they owned the place.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you have a techno party in an abandoned factory, then grab a döner from a food truck that plays live DJ sets. It’s a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You spot a true local if they still know where the legendary pink church used to be—nothing else has changed around here since the '90s.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a woman knitting on the T while a guy tap danced for tips. Only in SF does a yarn and rhythm combo unfold mid-commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think cafés in Gràcia are all about brunch and selfies, but locals know the best croissants are hidden in the back of a tiny bakery on Carrer de Verdi.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they mistakenly ask for 'tapas' in a café instead of 'pintxos' when they're in Gràcia.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'excuse me' on the bus. Locals perfected the art of the silent shuffle past each other.
Caught a group singing old 90s R&B on the 59 last night. They turned the bus into a club car until the driver started tapping the brakes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw the guy in a bathrobe walking his dog past the bakery, both looking completely unbothered by the world around them.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it’s normal to see spontaneous street art battles; walls become canvases overnight, transforming dull corners into vibrant galleries.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local if they can spot a busted BART train from a block away and still make it to the taqueria before it closes.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, I saw a guy pull out a whole saxophone during a Muni delay, turning the bus stop into an impromptu jazz concert. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the tiny plazas where locals sip their vermut and chat for hours.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion over which way to face on the metro. Locals always know to turn away from the doors.
